Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 (UNKNOWN - the form code reads Rev 0526; no year is printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The Tactical is a Model 870 set up for defence -- short barrel, extended magazine tube on most configurations, and often a different stock. RemArms's book covers the Model 870 platform and its strip is the same on your gun, with one thing to hold on to: the book was written around the standard tube, so where it counts shells or sends you into the magazine spring retainer, read it as a description of the plain gun and not a statement about the tube on yours. The mechanical procedure is unchanged; the magazine is not.

steps.title: Cross-bolt safety in, red band hidden
steps.action: Before anything else, push the safety button through from the left so the RED BAND cannot be seen. That is the safe position on an 870 and it is the position the whole strip is done in.
steps.prose: Cross-bolt button behind the trigger, same as every 870. If your Tactical has an oversized safety button fitted, it works the same way and the red band still tells you the truth -- but check it by looking, because an oversized button is easier to move by accident against a jacket.
steps.quote: To engage the safety mechanism, push the button so the RED BAND MARKING CANNOT BE SEEN.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — Important Parts of the Firearm - The Safety Mechanism, p.7
steps.warn: Even when the safety mechanism is engaged, careless handling can cause the firearm to fire.

steps.title: Action bar lock up, fore-end back
steps.action: Push upward on the action bar lock -- the small lever inside the front of the trigger guard -- and pull the fore-end rearward to open the action.
steps.prose: With the hammer down the fore-end is locked forward; the action bar lock is what releases it. This is the single motion that trips up owners coming off a gun with a slide release button on the outside of the trigger guard: on an 870 you reach INSIDE the guard for it.
steps.quote: TO OPEN THE ACTION: 1. Push upward on the action bar lock. See Picture 4. 2. Pull the fore-end rearward to open the action.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — Important Parts of the Firearm - The Fore-End, p.8

steps.title: Empty the magazine as well as the chamber
steps.action: Work the action slowly to bring each shell to the ejection port and lift it out, then keep cycling until the magazine is empty. Then look into the ejection port and check chamber AND magazine.
steps.prose: A pump gun holds its shells where you cannot see them. Racking once empties the chamber and immediately feeds another round from the tube, so a single cycle is not unloading -- it is reloading. Cycle until the carrier comes up bare, then look.
steps.quote: III. TO UNLOAD THE FIREARM: 1. Point the firearm in a safe direction. 2. Engage the safety mechanism. RED BAND WILL NOT SHOW. 3. Push upward on the action bar lock. 4. Pull the fore-end slowly rearward until the front of the shell is even with the ejection port.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Load And Unload, p.11
steps.warn: Look into the ejection port. Check the chamber and magazine to make sure there are no shells in the firearm.

steps.title: Read the barrel marking, not the box
steps.action: Check the gauge and chamber length stamped on the barrel and never use ammunition that exceeds the chamber length shown there.
steps.prose: RemArms puts the answer on the barrel because the receiver cannot tell you: 870 barrels swap between guns, so the barrel on the bench is the only authority for what the gun in your hands is chambered for. Read it now, while the gun is open and empty, rather than at the moment you are loading it.
steps.quote: WARNING! BEFORE LOADING, ALWAYS CHECK THE BARREL MARKING FOR THE CORRECT GAUGE AND CHAMBER LENGTH. NEVER USE AMMUNITION WHICH EXCEEDS THE CHAMBER LENGTH SHOWN ON THE BARREL.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — The Barrel - Barrel Interchangeability, p.9

steps.title: Safety on, action open, then fore-end forward about halfway
steps.action: Start the strip proper with the safety engaged and the action opened on the action bar lock, then slide the fore-end forward approximately halfway.
steps.prose: Halfway is not approximate for the sake of it -- it is the position where the action bars sit clear of the shell latches and the barrel guide ring is off the seat, which is what lets the barrel come out in the next two moves. Fully forward or fully back and the barrel will not lift.
steps.quote: 1. Engage the safety mechanism. RED BAND WILL NOT SHOW. 2. Push the action bar lock upward and pull the fore-end rearward to open the action.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.12
steps.warn: Look into the ejection port and check the chamber and magazine to make sure there are no shells in the firearm.

steps.title: Fore-end to the halfway position
steps.action: Slide the fore-end forward approximately halfway and leave it there.
steps.prose: Halfway, and on a Tactical that position matters more than usual: an extended magazine tube is held by a clamp or a barrel-clamp band at the muzzle end on many configurations, and the fore-end has to be clear of it before the barrel moves. If a clamp is fitted, loosen it before you try to draw the barrel.
steps.quote: 3. Slide the fore-end forward approximately halfway.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.12

steps.title: Unscrew the magazine cap
steps.action: Unscrew and remove the magazine cap from the end of the magazine tube.
steps.prose: Here is the real difference on this row. On a plain 870 the magazine cap threads onto the end of the standard tube. On a Tactical with a factory extension the cap is at the muzzle end of a longer tube, or an extension nut replaces it altogether. RemArms's book describes the standard arrangement; take the barrel off however your own tube is capped, and do not force a cap that is actually an extension nut.
steps.quote: 4. Unscrew and remove the magazine cap.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.12

steps.title: Barrel forward and off
steps.action: Take hold of the barrel ahead of the magazine tube and pull the barrel from the receiver.
steps.prose: Hold it ahead of the tube, not by the muzzle, so the barrel guide ring comes off the magazine tube square. It should draw straight forward with no twisting; if it binds, the fore-end has crept out of the halfway position and the ejector is still in the barrel's cut.
steps.quote: 5. Take hold of the barrel ahead of the magazine tube and pull the barrel from the receiver.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.12

steps.title: Field strip complete -- barrel, magazine cap, receiver
steps.action: Barrel off, magazine cap off, receiver with the fore-end still on the tube. That is the whole field strip for cleaning, and with the barrel off the action must be left alone.
steps.prose: Everything routine is reachable from here: the bore from the chamber end, the locking notch in the barrel, the breech face and the inside of the receiver. Going further is the deep clean, and RemArms publishes it -- fore-end, bolt and slide, and the trigger plate -- but nothing on this gun needs it after an ordinary day's shooting.
steps.quote: WARNING! DO NOT pump the action or pull the trigger repeatedly with the barrel removed.
steps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Assemble, p.10

deepSteps.title: Carrier up, left shell latch held down
deepSteps.action: With the barrel already off, push the carrier upward, reach into the bottom of the receiver and depress and hold the left shell latch.
deepSteps.prose: The left shell latch stands in the path of the action bar sleeve, and until it is held flat the fore-end assembly will not come off the tube. This is the step people force. A fingertip is enough; if it needs pressure you are on the carrier, not the latch.
deepSteps.quote: 6. Push the carrier upward. 7. Reach into the bottom of the receiver. Depress and hold the left shell latch. See Picture 14.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.12

deepSteps.title: Fore-end assembly forward off the magazine tube
deepSteps.action: Holding the latch down, slide the fore-end forward and off the magazine tube. If the top right edge of the slide binds on the bottom front edge of the ejection port, push the front end of the bolt down to free it.
deepSteps.prose: RemArms documents the bind because it is normal, not a fault -- the slide's top corner catches the port lip on nearly every 870 at some point in its travel. Pushing the front of the bolt down drops that corner below the lip and the whole assembly walks off the tube. Never lever it.
deepSteps.quote: 8. Slide the fore-end forward and off of the magazine tube. NOTE: The top right edge of the slide may bind on the bottom front edge of the ejection port in the receiver. To free the slide, push the front end of the bolt down. See Picture 15.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.12

deepSteps.title: Breech bolt and slide off the action bars
deepSteps.action: Lift the breech bolt assembly and slide assembly off the rear of the action bars.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt and slide sit on the back of the bars and are located there rather than latched, so once the assembly is out of the receiver they lift straight off. Keep them together as a unit -- the book cleans them as a unit and there is nothing inside either that an owner is asked to open.
deepSteps.quote: 9. Lift the breech bolt assembly and slide assembly from the rear of the action bars.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.12

deepSteps.title: Steps 10 to 12 are Super Magnum only -- skip them
deepSteps.action: A Tactical is not a Super Magnum, so the port cover steps are not yours -- your bolt has no port cover. Skip straight from lifting the bolt and slide off the action bars to the trigger plate pins.
deepSteps.prose: This is the one place the Model 870 book branches, and it branches by name. If your bolt has no port cover on it, there is nothing to lift a tab under and nothing to slide rearward; the next thing you do is tap out the trigger plate pins.
deepSteps.aside: The parts list says the same thing from the other end: parts marked with an asterisk there are for the Super Magnum only and are not interchangeable with any other Model 870.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: Steps 10-12 are for the Model 870™ Super Magnum ONLY.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.13

deepSteps.title: Tap out the two trigger plate pins
deepSteps.action: Tap out the front and rear trigger plate pins with a punch of the right diameter, working from one side only.
deepSteps.prose: They are a push fit with detent springs in the receiver, so they need a tap rather than a shove, and a punch that is a hair too small will start to bell the pin head. Push them out to the same side each time; they go back the way they came.
deepSteps.quote: 13. Tap out the front and rear trigger plate pins. See Picture 15.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.13

deepSteps.title: Trigger plate assembly out -- and keep the safety on while it comes
deepSteps.action: Lift the rear of the trigger plate assembly, slide it rearward and remove it from the receiver. Keep the safety mechanism engaged the whole time.
deepSteps.prose: The hammer is cocked and under mainspring tension in the plate you are holding. With the safety engaged the trigger cannot release it; with the safety off, a knock is enough. This is why the book asks for the safety at every stage rather than only during clearing.
deepSteps.quote: 14. Lift the rear of the trigger plate assembly, slide rearward and remove from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Disassemble, p.13
deepSteps.warn: DO NOT allow the hammer to snap forward when the trigger plated is removed.

deepSteps.title: The magazine plug section is written for the standard tube -- check yours before you go in
deepSteps.action: If you need to fit or remove a magazine plug for migratory bird hunting, note first that the book describes two different magazine spring retainers -- one with a round hole in the centre, one with a slot -- and that either is under full spring tension. On an extended tube the retainer sits at the far end of a longer, stronger spring.
deepSteps.prose: This is the one job on an 870 that reliably hurts people, and an extension makes it worse rather than better: more spring, more stored energy, and a retainer that leaves at speed. Eye protection and a hand over the end of the tube, every time. If your tube is capped by an extension nut rather than a magazine cap, the book's procedure is not describing your gun's front end.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: There are two types of magazine spring retainers used in the Model 870™ shotgun. One has a round hole in the center, the other has a slot in the center.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — To Assemble The Magazine Plug, p.11
deepSteps.warn: Always wear eye protection and use extreme care when removing the magazine spring retainer, as the retainer is under tension from the magazine spring.

deepSteps.title: Trigger plate: oil only, and let it stand
deepSteps.action: Clean the trigger plate assembly as a unit with oil only. Spray it, let it stand for fifteen minutes, spray again to wash the components off, then shake off the excess lubricant.
deepSteps.prose: Oil only, and as a unit -- this is the one assembly RemArms tells you not to take apart and not to put solvent through. Solvent flushes the residue into the trigger plate and leaves it there dry; oil carries it back out. The fifteen-minute stand is what does the work, so do not rush it.
deepSteps.quote: Spray the trigger plate assembly with oil as shown. See Picture 18. Let stand for 15 minutes. Spray again to wash off components. Shake off excess lubricant.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — Lubrication And Maintenance, p.13
deepSteps.warn: Excessive use of a non-recommended lubricant could adversely affect the function and safe operation of your firearm.

deepSteps.title: Deep clean complete -- and the action bar lock check comes first on the way back
deepSteps.action: Before the trigger plate goes home, check that the end of the action bar lock is below the end of the left connector. Then seat the plate carrier-first, align the holes and tap the two pins back in.
deepSteps.prose: That one check is the difference between a gun that reassembles and a gun that fights you: if the action bar lock is sitting above the connector the plate will not drop into the receiver and forcing it bends the connector. Look, then fit.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Check to make sure that the end of the action bar lock is below the end of the left connector. See Picture 19.
deepSteps.cite:
Owner's Manual
Instruction Book for:
Model 870 & 870 Super Magnum
Pump Action Shotguns — Form RD 7058 Rev 0526 — How To Reassemble, p.14

cleaning.name: BORE, LOCKING NOTCH & CHOKE TUBE
tasks: Select the correct gauge cleaning brush, wet it with solvent and push the rod through the barrel several times
Follow with correctly sized patches, repeating with a clean patch each time until the patch comes out clean
Remove all shooting residue from the locking notch in the barrel -- this is the seat the bolt locks into and it is the spot most owners miss
On a short Tactical barrel the whole bore is one rod stroke, so slow down rather than speeding up, and work the chamber and forcing cone hardest
Remove the choke tube, clean it and its threads with solvent, wipe dry, oil the threads and refit -- and never fire the gun without a choke tube installed

cleaning.name: BREECH BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Clean the breech bolt assembly as a unit: brush with cleaning solvent, then wipe clean and dry
Brush the inside of the receiver with solvent and wipe it dry
Keep fingers covered or gloved inside the receiver -- RemArms warns there may be sharp edges in there
Work the extractor and the breech face, where the carbon ring builds

cleaning.name: TRIGGER PLATE, LUBRICATION & STORAGE
tasks: Trigger plate assembly: clean as a unit with OIL ONLY -- spray, stand fifteen minutes, spray again, shake off the excess
Avoid over-lubrication at all times; a thin coat of oil is all that is needed to prevent rusting

Wipe the outside with a lightly oiled cloth, and pay attention to the magazine extension and any clamp -- the joint between tube and extension traps moisture and is not somewhere you can see rust starting
For storage, clean the gun carefully and oil it thoroughly, and wipe the outside surfaces with a light coat of oil occasionally
Before shooting again, remove all excess lubrication and wipe the chamber and bore thoroughly dry

reassembly: Check that the end of the action bar lock is below the end of the left connector before the trigger plate goes anywhere near the receiver.
Insert the trigger plate assembly carrier first, align the holes and tap the front and rear trigger plate pins back in.
Place the fore-end assembly over the magazine tube, then set the slide block and breech bolt assemblies on the rear of the action bars.
Guide the action bars in until the right shell latch stops them, push the carrier up, depress and hold the right shell latch and slide the fore-end rearward; repeat for the left shell latch.
Slide the fore-end rearward until the action bar lock stops it, push the action bar lock up and bring the fore-end back to about halfway.
Align the ejector cut on the rear of the barrel with the ejector in the receiver, seat the barrel without forcing it against the ejector, then replace and tighten the magazine cap.
fncheck: With the barrel back on and the magazine cap tight, and the chamber and magazine confirmed empty: the fore-end should run the full stroke smoothly and the action bar lock should hold it forward with the hammer down; pushing the action bar lock up should release it every time; the safety should move through with a positive detent and show the red band on FIRE and hide it on SAFE; and the barrel should sit flush with no movement at the guide ring. RemArms asks that the gun be checked periodically by RemArms, LLC or a Remington authorized service center for inspection and replacement of worn or damaged parts.
